props.name: children
props.description: The parts of one file: `Attachment.Media` with an icon or a picture, `Attachment.Content` with the `Attachment.Title` and `Attachment.Description`, and `Attachment.Actions` with one `Attachment.Action` per action. An `Attachment.Trigger` goes before `Attachment.Actions`.

props.name: orientation
props.description: The layout, written to `data-orientation`. `horizontal` lays the media beside the content. `vertical` stacks a tile with the media on top, and its actions float in the media's top end corner on a `secondary` fill, so they stay visible on any photo.

props.name: size
props.description: The padding, the media and the text size.

props.name: state
props.description: The upload lifecycle, written to `data-state`. Your app picks and uploads the files, and sets `state` as the upload moves on. It only styles: `idle` dashes the border, `uploading` and `processing` sweep a highlight across the title and dim image media, and `error` tints the border, the media and the description with the error role. Under reduced motion, the title stays still. The error state is a colour, so say the state, and the reason an upload failed, in words in `Attachment.Description`.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The list's name. Give the group an `aria-label` or an `aria-labelledby`.

props.name: aria-labelledby
props.description: The ids of the elements that name the list, in place of `aria-label`.

props.name: children
props.description: The `Attachment.Root`s, each one an item of the list. They sit in one row that scrolls sideways and snaps to each attachment, and an edge fades while more attachments lie past it, on the side right-to-left text starts from too. Base UI measures those edges from its `DirectionProvider`, so in a right-to-left app, wrap the app in one as well as setting `dir`.

props.name: className

props.description: The threshold in pixels that must be passed before the overflow edge attributes are applied. Accepts a single number for all edges or an object to configure them individually.

props.name: style

props.name: variant
props.description: What the square holds, written to `data-variant`. `icon` holds an icon or a status glyph, such as a Loader. `image` frames an `img` placed directly inside the media in the square, which the image fills and crops to. Image media stays at 60% opacity until the root's `state` is `idle` or `done`. For another shape, put an `Attachment.AspectRatio` inside the media with one of AspectRatio's ratios.

props.name: children
props.description: The content, which fills the frame. Give an `img` or `video` `size-full object-cover`, so it crops to the frame instead of stretching. Round and fill the child, not the frame.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes. Give the frame a width, such as `w-full max-w-md`, and its height follows the ratio. An `aspect-*` class, such as `aspect-[7/5]`, replaces the ratio.

props.name: ratio
props.description: The frame's width to height, written to `data-ratio`. It is required. For a ratio outside the set, pass an `aspect-*` class in `className`.

props.name: children
props.description: The detail, such as the size, the progress or the reason an upload failed, such as "Upload failed. The file is over 10 MB." The root's `state` only styles, so write the state here in words.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The button's name, which says the action and the file, such as "Remove floor-plan.pdf". The type requires it, since the button holds only an icon.

props.name: children
props.description: The label and icons. Mark a leading icon with `data-icon="inline-start"` and a trailing one with `data-icon="inline-end"`, and that side takes the narrower icon padding. Your own icon components must pass `data-icon` through to the element they render. An SVG without a `size-*` class renders at 16px, or 12px at the `xs` and `icon-xs` sizes. Any `size-*` class opts out, `size-auto` included, and `w-*` or `h-*` alone does not. An SVG without a `viewBox` clips at that size instead of scaling. Give it `size-auto` to keep its own `width` and `height`, or restore the `viewBox`.

props.name: className
props.description: Extra classes, merged last through `cn`. A `px-*` class replaces the label padding only. The icon side keeps its own padding, which `has-data-[icon=inline-start]:pl-*` or `has-data-[icon=inline-end]:pr-*` replaces.

props.name: focusableWhenDisabled
props.description: Whether the button should be focusable when disabled.

props.name: isPending
props.description: Marks an action in flight. The button blocks activation, dims, and stamps `data-pending` and `aria-busy`. It stays in the focus order, so a keyboard user is still on it when the result arrives. `focusableWhenDisabled={false}` takes it out of the focus order. `aria-busy` announces nothing, so say what is happening in the label, such as "Saving", or in a `role="status"` region outside the button. Put a label that changes with the state in its own element, such as `{label}`: page translation replaces a bare text child with its own nodes, so React's update to the old text node never shows.

props.name: isVisuallyDisabled
props.description: Makes the button look and announce disabled while it stays interactive. It stamps `aria-disabled`, and an explicit `aria-disabled` wins. Click, keyboard and focus still work, and a Tooltip on the button still opens. Use it for an action that explains on activation why it is unavailable.

props.name: nativeButton
props.description: Whether the component renders a native `<button>` element when replacing it via the `render` prop. Set to `false` if the rendered element is not a button (for example, `<div>`).

props.name: onIntent
props.description: Fires once when the pointer's predicted path enters the inflated hit rect, for prefetching. Browsers without pointer prediction never fire it.

props.name: pendingIndicator
props.description: What a pending button shows in its leading icon position. When you omit it, a spinner shows there and the button's leading and bare icons hide, while a `data-icon="inline-end"` icon stays. A node replaces the spinner and does not animate on its own. `null` or `false` shows nothing and hides nothing, so the call site draws its own pending state. Fade that content with `group-data-pending/button:opacity-0`, not `invisible`, which drops the label from the accessible name, and give an overlay no `data-icon`.

props.name: predictionZoneSize
props.description: Pixels added to every side of the hit rect when predicting pointer intent.

props.description: Allows you to replace the component's HTML element with a different tag, or compose it with another component. Accepts a `ReactElement` or a function that returns the element to render.

props.name: style
props.description: Style applied to the element, or a function that returns a style object based on the component's state.

props.name: variant
props.description: The fill and text colour. The theme sets the `outline` border. `link` looks like an inline text link.

props.name: aria-label
props.description: The trigger's name, which says what activating it does, such as "Preview inspection-report.pdf". Give it one, since it holds no text of its own.

props.name: render
props.description: The element to render, a `<button type="button">` by default, so it never submits a form it sits in. `render={<a href="…" />}` makes it a link. A link takes no `disabled`, so mark an unavailable one `aria-disabled="true"`, and it cancels its own activation. A dialog's trigger composes it as it composes `Button`: `<Dialog.Trigger render={<Attachment.Trigger aria-label="Preview report.pdf" />} />`.
